A_target.statement:
Let $K$ be a [[Definition:Compact Space|compact space]] and $f: K \to \R$ [[Definition:Lower Semicontinuous|lower semicontinuous]].
Then $f$ attains its [[Definition:Infimum of Mapping|infimum]] on $K$, and for each $a \in \R$ the set $\set {x: \map f x \le a}$ is [[Definition:Closed Set (Topology)|closed]].

B_source.statement:
Let $K$ be a [[Definition:Compact Space|compact space]] and $g: K \to \R$ [[Definition:Upper Semicontinuous|upper semicontinuous]].
Then $g$ attains its [[Definition:Supremum of Mapping|supremum]] on $K$, and for each $a \in \R$ the set $\set {x: \map g x \ge a}$ is [[Definition:Closed Set (Topology)|closed]].

substitutions.the superlevel set where g is at least a: the sublevel set where f is at most -a

object_map.reformulation: Reverse the order on the codomain by negating, turning every statement about maxima into one about minima.

validity_conditions: Negation is an order-reversing involution on the extended reals, so it converts every upper bound statement into a lower bound statement.
Directly from the definitions, f is lower semicontinuous exactly when -f is upper semicontinuous.
Negation exchanges suprema with infima and superlevel sets with sublevel sets, so the entire upper semicontinuous theory mirrors onto the lower semicontinuous one with no new argument.
proof_plan:
Let $g = -f$.
As $f$ is lower semicontinuous, $\set {x: \map g x < a} = \set {x: \map f x > -a}$ is open for all $a$, so $g$ is [[Definition:Upper Semicontinuous|upper semicontinuous]].
By the source result, $g$ attains its supremum at some $x^* \in K$.

Then:
:$\map f {x^*} = -\map g {x^*} = -\sup g = \inf f$
so $f$ attains its infimum.

We have:
:$\set {x: \map f x \le a} = \set {x: \map g x \ge -a}$
which is closed by the source result.
{{qed}}
